questions.html: Which provides a common scripting language to web developers to design, test and deploy Internet Applications?
questions.hint: JavaScript was jointly introduced by Netscape and Sun Inc. on December 4, 1995 as a scripting language for web developers.

questions.html: Expand CGI:
questions.hint: CGI = Common Gateway Interface. JavaScript bridges the gap between HTML and complex CGI programs on the server.

questions.html: JavaScript programming language is used to develop:
questions.hint: JavaScript is used to develop Dynamic Web Pages (interactive pages) unlike static HTML pages.

questions.html: The Dynamic Web Page helps to save server's:
questions.hint: Data validation on the client side (JavaScript) saves server traffic — less load on the server.

questions.html: User entered data is validated before sending it to the server. This is called:
questions.hint: When JavaScript validates user data before sending to server, it creates a Dynamic Web Page interaction that reduces server load.

questions.html: JavaScript can be implemented using which tag?
questions.hint: JavaScript is implemented using <script>...</script> tags. It is recommended to place these in <head>.

questions.html: Expand DHTML:
options: a) Distance Hyper Text Markup Language
b) Dynamic Hyper Text Markup Language
c) Distance High Text Markup Language
d) Dynamic High Text Markup Language
questions.hint: DHTML = Dynamic Hyper Text Markup Language. It is HTML enhanced with JavaScript for dynamic/interactive web pages.

questions.html: How many attributes are specified for the <script> tag?
questions.hint: The <script> tag has 2 important attributes: language (specifies scripting language) and type (value: text/javascript).

questions.html: Which attribute is used to indicate the scripting language with value 'text/javascript'?
questions.hint: The 'type' attribute indicates the scripting language. Its value should be 'text/javascript'.

questions.html: The shortcut key to reload a file into the browser is:
questions.hint: F5 is the shortcut key to refresh/reload the current page in a browser.

questions.html: JavaScript ignores spaces that appear between:
questions.hint: JavaScript ignores spaces between tokens (identifiers, operators, punctuators, constants, keywords).

questions.html: A data value for a variable that appears directly in a program is called:
questions.hint: A literal is a fixed value (data value) that appears directly in source code. Examples: 250, 3.14, true, 'Hello'.

questions.html: Which dialog box is mostly used to give a warning message to users?
questions.hint: The Alert dialog box gives warning messages to users. It has only one button: OK.

questions.html: In the snippet: var x = 250 + 2 - 200; the value of x is:
Write the syntax of the <script> tag.
questions.answer:
The <script> tag is used to embed JavaScript in an HTML page. Syntax:

<script language='javascript' type='text/javascript'>
  JavaScript code here
</script>

Attributes:
- language: Specifies the scripting language (value: 'javascript'). Optional in recent HTML versions.
- type: Indicates the scripting language (value: 'text/javascript').

The <script> tag can be placed anywhere in the HTML page but is recommended to be placed in the <head> section.
questions.hint: <script language='javascript' type='text/javascript'>JS code</script>. Two attributes: language and type. Best in <head>.

questions.html: What is the scope of variables? What are the types of scope?
questions.answer:
The scope of a variable is the lifetime of the variable — the region of source code in which it is defined and accessible.

Two types of scope:
1. Global Scope: A global variable is declared outside any function. It can be used and accessed everywhere in the JavaScript code — both inside and outside functions.

2. Local Scope: Variables declared within a function are defined only within the body of that function. They are local variables and can only be accessed inside that function. They cease to exist when the function ends.
questions.hint: Scope = lifetime of a variable. Global scope = accessible everywhere (declared outside functions). Local scope = only inside the function where declared.

questions.html: What is conditional operator? Give a suitable example.
questions.hint: Ternary operator: var x = (condition) ? value_if_true : value_if_false. Example: var result = (10>15) ? 100 : 150; → result = 150 (condition false).

questions.html: What are the comments in JavaScript?
questions.answer:
Comments in JavaScript are remarks or notes in source code that are ignored by the JavaScript interpreter — they do not affect execution. Comments make code more readable.

Two types:
1. Single-line comment: Begins with a double slash (//). Everything from // to the end of the line is ignored.
Example: // This is a single line comment

2. Multi-line comment: Begins with /* and ends with */. Everything between these is ignored, even across multiple lines.
Example:
/* This is a
multi-line comment */
questions.hint: Two types: Single-line (// to end of line) and Multi-line (/* ... */). Ignored by interpreter. Make code readable.

questions.html: What is the use of the Prompt dialog box?
questions.hint: Prompt = gets user input via a text box. Two parameters: message label + default value. OK returns the entered value; Cancel returns null.

questions.html: What are the advantages of JavaScript programming language?
questions.answer:
Advantages of JavaScript:

1. Dynamic Web Pages: HTML creates static web pages. JavaScript makes web pages interactive and dynamic — responding to user actions like clicks, form inputs, etc.

2. Client-side Validation: User-entered data in forms can be validated before sending to the server. This saves server traffic and reduces load on the server. Example: checking that an email field contains '@'.

3. Rich Interface: JavaScript provides rich UI elements such as textboxes, buttons, drag-and-drop components, sliders, and tooltips, giving site visitors an engaging experience. Example: creating a new email account interface.

4. Bridging HTML and CGI: JavaScript bridges the gap between simple HTML and complex CGI server-side programs, giving web developers a common tool.

5. Fast Execution: JavaScript executes on the client side (browser) — no server round-trip needed for most operations, resulting in faster response.
questions.hint: 5 advantages: Dynamic Web Pages (interactive), client-side validation (saves server load), rich interface (textboxes/sliders), bridges HTML and CGI, fast client-side execution.

questions.html: Briefly explain the basic data types in JavaScript.
questions.hint: Three types: String (characters in quotes), Number (integer or float), Boolean (true/false). JavaScript is dynamically typed — no type declaration needed.

questions.html: Explain the increment and decrement operators in JavaScript.
questions.answer:
Increment and Decrement operators change the value of a variable by 1.

Increment operator (++): Adds 1 to the operand. Two forms:
- Pre-increment (++m): Increments the operand FIRST, then returns the incremented value.
  var m = 1, n = ++m; // m = 2, n = 2
- Post-increment (m++): Returns the current value FIRST, then increments.
  var m = 1, n = m++; // m = 2, n = 1

Decrement operator (--): Subtracts 1 from the operand. Two forms:
- Pre-decrement (--m): Decrements FIRST, then returns the decremented value.
  var m = 2, n = --m; // m = 1, n = 1
- Post-decrement (m--): Returns current value FIRST, then decrements.
  var m = 2, n = m--; // n = 2, then m = 1

Key difference: Pre = change first, then use. Post = use first, then change.
questions.hint: ++ adds 1, -- subtracts 1. Pre-increment (++m): change first, then use. Post-increment (m++): use first, then change. Give all 4 examples with values.

questions.html: Explain the popup dialog boxes in JavaScript.
questions.hint: 3 dialog boxes: Alert (warning, OK only), Confirm (consent, OK=true/Cancel=false), Prompt (get input, OK=text/Cancel=null). For each: purpose, syntax, example, use case.

questions.hint: 5 operators: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (divide), % (modulus/remainder). Include shorthand (+=,-=,*=,/=,%=). Write complete JavaScript program with document.write().
